newsitem.title: USA: First of America to cut 400 jobs in Q1.
newsitem.headline: First of America to cut 400 jobs in Q1.

text.p: First of America Bank Corp said Tuesday that, as part of its ongoing restructuring, it will notify 400 employees by the end of the first quarter that their jobs are being eliminated.
Severance costs for the employees are expected to be between $4.0 million and $5.0 million.

First of America said its total full-time equivalent employees were 12,148 as of December 31, down 586 from year-end 1995. The 1996 total included 200 employees who have been notified that their positions were eliminated as part of the restructuring.
Jennifer Cox, senior vice president of the accounting division, said the severance costs will be taken as a charge in the first quarter.
She added that no further job cuts are expected.

Earlier, First of America reported fourth quarter earnings of $1.38 a share, up from $1.04 a year ago. Excluding one-time items, including gains on the sale or branches and charges for severance and write-downs, the bank earned $1.22 a share, up from $0.90 a year ago.

First of America, a $22 billion bank holding company, said its fourth quarter net interest income, on a fully taxable equivalent basis, was $230.2 million, down from $231.1 million a year ago but up slightly from the third quarter.
For the fourth quarter, non-interest revenue increased 29.2 percent to $130.2 million.
